held.title: Replacing the typed `WorkspaceError` with a plain string error breaks callers that downcast it
held.body:
`find_target` used to return `WorkspaceError::MissingPyprojectToml` wrapped in `anyhow::Error`, so callers could recognise it with `err.downcast_ref::<WorkspaceError>()`. The new code builds a fresh `anyhow!("...")` message from it, which drops the type. Any caller that downcasts this error stops matching, and its special handling is silently skipped. The non-strict `uv version` fallback to `uv self version` in the command dispatcher is the likely case.

I could not see whether such a downcast still exists; the `*_fallback_missing_strict*` test names suggest it once did. If it does, keep the type: attach the hint as context on the original error, or add the hint where the error is reported. Then `downcast_ref::<WorkspaceError>()` still succeeds.
